item.text: {"source_id":"train-361-4","response_sha256":"2d5c064c3a10087c0f4c87b13ad78c3d93b96842fa8e2941788ca3879a99bab6","status":"supported_error","reference_review_needed":false,"evidence_quote":"Since the ship had already covered 600 kilometers and then was blown backward by \\( D - 600 \\) kilometers, the remaining distance is one-third of the total distance \\( D \\):\n\\[ D - 600 = \\frac{D}{3} \\]","evidence_start":null,"evidence_end":null,"evidence_occurrence":1,"question_evidence_quote":"sailed his ship halfway to the destination by traveling due east for 20 hours at a speed of 30 kilometers per hour","observed_error":"The response identifies the backward displacement as D - 600 and sets that quantity equal to D/3.","violated_condition":"The initial 600 kilometers equals D/2; the post-storm progress equals D/3, so the westward displacement equals 600 - D/3.","error_description":"The response treats D − 600 as the storm's westward displacement and equates it to D/3. The initial 600 kilometers was half the total journey, while D/3 describes progress from the starting point after the storm. The displacement must be the difference between those positions; the subsequent algebra correctly executes an incorrect equation.","reference_review_reason":null,"secondary_errors":[],"uncertainty_note":null}
